# Thermopylae Aerospace Raises $1.6M to Build Low-Cost Interceptor Drones for Ukraine’s Air Defense

The startup, founded by a 21-year-old Ukrainian engineer, is building sub-$10,000 interceptors and plans to move operations to Ukraine for frontline testing

#### Aaron Thomasson

 01 Dec 2025 — 3 min read 

Thermopylae Aerospace Co-Founder & CEO Yehor Balytskyi

KYIV, Ukraine — 1 December 2025

Thermopylae Aerospace, a Ukrainian-led interceptor drone startup founded by 21-year-old engineer Yehor Balytskyi, has raised $1.6 million in pre-seed funding to develop and test a new low-cost air defense platform for Ukraine.

The round was led by investor Naval Ravikant, with participation from Founders, Inc., UA1 VC, Norgard Capital, and angel investors from SGA Capital, Cyrus Ventures and others, according to the company. In announcing the funding, Balytskyi described the company’s mission as delivering “new capabilities to our air defense groups with a novel interceptor platform.”

Thermopylae is developing an ultra-light, foldable quadcopter interceptor designed to counter glide bombs and Group 2 drones such as Shaheds. Launched from a standard mortar-like tube, the system uses thermal guidance and an electric motor to reach speeds of up to 350 km/h with a targeted flight time of up to 20 minutes. # SPART: The 21-Year-Old’s $10,000 Answer to the Shahed

by Connor Kerr | Aug 20, 2026 | Military Aviation, News | 0 comments

Somewhere over Ukraine tonight, a lawnmower engine bolted to a warhead is droning toward a city. It is called a Shahed-136, Russia stamps out its own copies as the Geran-2, and it costs somewhere between twenty and fifty thousand dollars. The problem has never been shooting one down. The problem is the receipt. Firing a $4 million Patriot missile at a $30,000 flying moped is the kind of maths that wins the battle and loses the war.

Now a 21-year-old wants to fix that with something that launches like a potato gun.

Quick Facts

- Product: SPART, a pneumatically launched, foldable quadcopter interceptor drone
- Founder: Yehor Balytskyi, a self-taught Ukrainian engineer (left Ukraine at 17 in 2022, now ~21), CEO of Thermopylae Aerospace; co-founder Carter Scherer
- Cost: Designed for high-volume manufacture at roughly under US$10,000 per unit
- Method: Thermal-guided; flies into large attack drones (Group 2 threats such as the Shahed) rather than using an expensive rocket-motor missile; recoverable if it misses
- Speed / endurance: Up to 350 km/h (217 mph); up to ~20 minutes flight time
- Backing: California startup founded June 2025; raised US$1.6M pre-seed (Nov 2025) from Naval Ravikant and Ukraine-focused VC UA1; grew from 2 to ~5 people
- Venue: End-to-end demo at Edwards Air Force Base during Game of Drones 26-2 (16 July 2026), briefing Air Force

# Why This San Francisco Startup Built A Jet Interceptor In Two Weeks

 Wednesday, August 26, 2026 By Rafael Chen technology 4 min read 

Building military hardware usually takes decades, billions of dollars, and endless bureaucratic loops. A two-person team in San Francisco just threw that playbook out the window. IMPACT Drones, a Y Combinator-backed startup, claims they engineered a working prototype of a high-speed jet interceptor named SABLE in a staggering fourteen days. 

When low-cost attack drones start slamming into commercial data centers, power grids, and civilian airports, traditional defense timelines stop making sense. You cannot wait seven years for a legacy prime contractor to deliver a missile that costs two million dollars to shoot down a thirty-thousand-dollar threat. The economics are broken, and modern software-first founders are capitalizing on the mismatch.

The sheer speed of the SABLE prototype build caught the aerospace industry off guard. Co-founders Jasper Lortije and Alessandro Fiume shared updates on social media highlighting that their newly incorporated company pulled off the feat just weeks after entering their incubator batch.
